The '''2019–20 Süper Lig''', officially called the '''Süper Lig Cemil Usta season''', was the 62nd season of the [[Süper Lig]], the highest tier [[Association football|football]] league of [[Turkey]]. The season was named after [[Cemil Usta]], a former Turkey national team player and [[Trabzonspor]] legend.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=285&ftxtID=31586 |title=Spor Toto Süper Lig'de Cemil Usta sezonu|website=tff.org |publisher=[[Turkish Football Federation]] |access-date=28 June 2019|language=tr }}</ref> [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] were the defending champions. Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey|coronavirus pandemic]], [[Ministry of Youth and Sports (Turkey)|The Ministry of Youth and Sports]] announced on 12 March 2020 that matches would be played [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] until the end of April,<ref>{{cite news |publisher= Hürriyet|date= 12 March 2020|title= Türkiye'de o tarihe kadar tüm spor müsabakaları seyircisiz oynanacak|url= https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/sporarena/resmi-aciklama-geldi-turkiyede-nisan-sonuna-kadar-tum-spor-musabakalari-seyircisiz-oynanacak-41467734|language=tr |access-date= 12 March 2020}}</ref> before indefinitely suspending matches altogether on 19 March.<ref>{{cite news |publisher= Hürriyet|date= 19 March 2020|title= Süper Lig'de maçlar ertelendi!|url= https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/sporarena/son-dakika-super-ligde-maclar-ertelendi-lig-ne-zaman-baslayacak-41472798|language=tr |access-date= 19 March 2020}}</ref> After a hiatus of nearly three months, the season resumed behind closed doors on 12 June 2020, with eight rounds still to play.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Football: Turkish soccer season restarts after almost three-month suspension {{!}} The Star|url=https://www.thestar.com.my/sport/football/2020/06/12/turkish-soccer-season-restarts-after-almost-three-month-suspension|access-date=12 June 2020|website=www.thestar.com.my}}</ref> The season ended with matches played on 26 July 2020, and without relegations.

[[İstanbul Başakşehir F.K.|Başakşehir]] clinched their first league title, on July 20, 2020 with a 1–0 win against [[Kayserispor]], one week to spare.

==Teams==
A total of 18 teams contested the league, including 15 sides from the [[2018–19 Süper Lig|2018–19 season]] and three promoted from the [[2018–19 TFF First League]]. It included [[Denizlispor]] and [[Gençlerbirliği S.K.|Gençlerbirliği]], the top two teams from the [[TFF First League]], and [[Gaziantep F.K.|Gaziantep]], the winners of the [[2018–19 TFF First League#Promotion Playoffs|2018–19 TFF First League playoffs]].
[[Akhisar Belediyespor|Akhisarspor]], [[Büyükşehir Belediye Erzurumspor|BB Erzurumspor]], and [[Bursaspor]] were relegated to the [[2019–20 TFF First League]]. Gençlerbirliği made an immediate return to the top level, Denizlispor returned to it after nine years and Gaziantep made their debut. Erzurum BB were immediately relegated to the second level. Akhisarspor ended seven years at the top level. Bursaspor were relegated after spending 13 years in the top flight. During this period, they were champions of the [[2009–10 Süper Lig]].
